It distinguishes itself from siblings like [3DGS-DR](1471-3dgs-dr.md) and [Relightable 3D Gaussian](6001-relightable-3d-gaussian.md) by explicitly storing incident lighting and BRDF parameters per Gaussian, facilitating direct lighting reconstruction via environment maps and indirect lighting via spherical harmonics [S1][S2, unofficial].

The claim states that the method distinguishes itself by storing incident lighting and BRDF parameters per Gaussian, facilitating direct lighting reconstruction via environment maps and indirect lighting via spherical harmonics. Both Source [S1] and Source [S2] explicitly state that Gao et al. (the method in question) embeds BRDF parameters (albedo, roughness, surface normals, and incident lighting) into each Gaussian. Furthermore, both sources confirm that direct lighting is reconstructed using environment maps and indirect lighting is modeled using spherical harmonics. The claim accurately reflects the facts presented in the evidence.

These mechanisms (environment maps for direct lighting and SH for indirect) are the standard technical means for achieving physically based rendering and relighting, which inherently involves capturing specular highlights and diffuse reflections. Therefore, the claim that the evidence supports the ability to enable physically based rendering and relighting is accurate based on the provided text.
